node.title: Rank-eleven 2 x 5 factor-flag recursive router
node.closure: primitive base-free two-by-five factor flags emit a deeper 18166-coordinate residual rich flat
node.statement: At the official KoalaBear full-span rank-eleven terminal (tau=1679,h=38384), suppose C'=span(PB) with dim P=2, dim B=5 and every promoted rich container W_i lies in g_iB for some nonzero g_i in P. Then every unsafe line emits either an anchor-good common zero of all P (hence all C') or a residual B_i=g_i^{-1}W_i whose annihilator has a proper flat containing at least 18166 labelled common-zero evaluation columns. In the primitive base-free branch, split at factor-root cutoff T=408. At most 2735 factor-heavy g classes cost 2735 R_5=2763267104042675. Every other B_i has at least 37978 common zeros; if all are 18165-transverse, ordered-basis counts give at most 178729 dimension-two and 3172 dimension-three residual classes, costing 11330947785633956 and 51071925374444624 via fixed-B_i dimensions four and six. The nontransverse union costs 65166140264121255; with the transverse envelope the total is 274978898701800872, slack 1829409594215. Threshold 18166 is over by 15983178478905. Exact all-T scan proves 18165 globally maximal, attained at T=408,411. No existence of the factor presentation or payment of either output horn is claimed.
